api/Global.LHH_TestSDK.html.title: Class LHH_TestSDK | LHH Test SDK
api/Global.LHH_TestSDK.html.summary: Class LHH_TestSDK Entry point for automated tests against a device build from the Unity Editor (NUnit, Edit Mode or Play Mode). Inheritance Object LHH_TestSDK Namespace: Global Assembly: LHH.TestSDK.Docs.dll Syntax public sealed class LHH_TestSDK : MonoBehaviour Remarks First API call on a run: connect to Test Controller, lease device, Appium session, wait for player hub. Configure via menu LHH Test SDK - Settings (gRPC, platform, app path, bundle id). Requires LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST and a running Test Controller. Editor-only; not in player builds. Methods CleanUpAfterTest() Returns the leased device to the Test Controller and resets setup state for the next run. Declaration public static void CleanUpAfterTest() Remarks Called automatically when the Unity Test Runner finishes a run or reports a runner error. Manual calls are rarely needed; use only if you run tests outside the Test Runner or need early teardown. ClickButton(string, float) Waits for a UI object, then invokes its Unity UI Button onClick in the running game. Declaration public static Task ClickButton(string buttonPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string buttonPath Hierarchy path with / separators (root via GameObject.Find, children via Transform.Find). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait for the button object before failing. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use, then WaitForObject(buttonPath) before click. Not for native store UI; use PurchaseByButton for IAP buy buttons. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton( "PopupManager/ShopConfirmPopup(Clone)/Panel/Background/Button Confirm"); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, hub command failed, or click could not run. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. GetGameData(string) Reads PlayerPrefs from the game player for the given key (returned as string). Declaration public static Task<string> GetGameData(string key) Parameters Type Name Description string key PlayerPrefs key, e.g. coin or heart. Returns Type Description Task<string> Int, float, or string value encoded as string (player tries int, then float, then string). Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use. Parse in tests with int.TryParse etc. Examples string raw = await LHH_TestSDK.GetGameData("coin"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(raw, out int coins)); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed or the player could not read the key. GetText(string, float) Waits for a UI object, then reads displayed text from the running game player. Declaration public static Task<string> GetText(string textPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string textPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as ClickButton and WaitForObject). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait for the object before failing. Returns Type Description Task<string> Text content reported by the player for the object at textPath. Remarks Runs implicit setup on first use, then WaitForObject(textPath) before reading. Supports Unity UI Text and TextMeshPro on the target GameObject. Examples string label = await LHH_TestSDK.GetText("HUD/CoinLabel"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(label, out int coins)); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, hub command failed, or text could not be read. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. LogError(string) Writes a message to the Unity Console in red (calls LogWithColor with red). Declaration public static void LogError(string message) Parameters Type Name Description string message Text to log. Remarks Use for assertion detail without failing the test until you call NUnit Assert. LogWithColor(string, Color) Writes a message to the Unity Console with the given color (rich text). Declaration public static void LogWithColor(string message, Color color) Parameters Type Name Description string message Text to log. Color color Color applied to the message in the Console window. Remarks Does not contact the Test Controller; safe to use anywhere in a test. Purchase(string) Starts in-app purchase by store catalog product id (no in-game button click). Declaration public static Task Purchase(string catalogProductId) Parameters Type Name Description string catalogProductId IAP product id configured in the game. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Controller sends purchase to the Unity player, then drives the native store sheet. Prefer PurchaseByButton when the test must tap a shop UI element. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.Purchase("com.example.coins_1000"); Exceptions Type Condition ArgumentException catalogProductId is null or whitespace. InvalidOperationException Setup failed, purchase failed, or timed out (3 minutes). PurchaseByButton(string) Clicks an in-game shop buy button and completes purchase via the native store UI. Declaration public static Task<bool> PurchaseByButton(string buttonPath) Parameters Type Name Description string buttonPath Hierarchy path to a Unity UI Button (same format as WaitForObject). Returns Type Description Task<bool> True if the Test Controller reports success; false otherwise. Remarks Controller taps the button, waits for the IAP sheet, and confirms buy. Use ClickButton for non-IAP UI. Use Purchase when you have a catalog product id instead of a button path. Examples bool ok = await LHH_TestSDK.PurchaseByButton( "__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Button Buy"); Assert.IsTrue(ok); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Setup failed, or the purchase client is not initialized. WaitForObject(string, float) Blocks until a GameObject exists in the game player hierarchy at the given path. Declaration public static Task WaitForObject(string objectPath, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string objectPath Hierarchy path with / separators (same rules as ClickButton). float timeoutSeconds Maximum seconds to wait before throwing. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Polls every 2 seconds. Runs implicit setup on first use. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager", timeoutSeconds: 30f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Implicit setup failed. TimeoutException Object not found before timeoutSeconds elapses. WaitForScene(string, float) Blocks until a loaded scene with the given name is active in the game player. Declaration public static Task WaitForScene(string waitScene, float timeoutSeconds = 30) Parameters Type Name Description string waitScene Scene name to match (case-sensitive), compared against all currently loaded scenes. float timeoutSeconds Maximum time to wait before failing the test. Returns Type Description Task Remarks Polls every 2 seconds. Runs implicit setup on first use. Examples await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); Exceptions Type Condition InvalidOperationException Implicit setup failed. TimeoutException No matching scene before timeoutSeconds elapses.

index.html.title: LHH Test SDK | LHH Test SDK
index.html.summary: LHH Test SDK Use LHH_TestSDK from NUnit tests in the Unity Editor to drive a real Android device build through the Test Controller: game UI, waits, PlayerPrefs checks, and in-app purchases. iOS is not supported yet. Section Purpose Manual Install SDK, controller, write and run tests (for QA) Scripting API Generated reference for LHH_TestSDK from XML doc comments in code Before you write tests Add com.lhh.testsdk from Bitbucket and run Install Test SDK in LHH Test SDK → Settings. Install and Run Test Server from the same window (Advance Settings). Set gRPC address, Android app path (.apk), and bundle id; use an APK that includes InAppTestRunner. Start with the Manual. Quick example [Test] public async Task Shop_opens_on_home() { await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager"); await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton("__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Open Shop"); } Requires Unity 2022.3.67f2 or newer.

manual/install-sdk.html.title: Install the Test SDK | LHH Test SDK
manual/install-sdk.html.summary: Install the Test SDK This guide is for QA writing NUnit tests in the Unity Editor with LHH_TestSDK. Platform support: Android only today. iOS options in Settings are reserved for a later release—do not rely on iOS until documented otherwise. Requirements Unity 2022.3 or newer (2022.3.67f2+ recommended). A game project where the player build includes automation (see Player build below). Bitbucket SSH access to LiHuHu repos (for UPM git URLs). 1. Add the Test SDK package In the game project, edit Packages/manifest.json and add: "com.lhh.testsdk": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-sdk.git?path=Assets/TestSDK" Pin a release when dev specifies one, for example: "com.lhh.testsdk": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-sdk.git?path=Assets/TestSDK#v0.1.0" Open the project in Unity and wait for Package Manager to resolve the package. 2. Run Install Test SDK in the Editor Open LHH Test SDK → Settings. Enable Show Advance Settings. Click Install Test SDK and wait until progress shows Test SDK install finished. This step: Writes NuGet config under Assets/ and restores client packages (MagicOnion, MemoryPack, gRPC, etc.). Merges required Unity Package Manager dependencies into Packages/manifest.json. Adds the LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST scripting define so LHH_TestSDK and player hub code compile. You only need to run Install Test SDK again after a SDK update (see Updating after a release). 3. com.lhh.testcontroller.shared (required) The shared contracts package (com.lhh.testcontroller.shared) is not something QA normally adds by hand. Install Test SDK merges it into manifest.json, for example: "com.lhh.testcontroller.shared": "git@bitbucket.org:lihuhu/lhh-auto-test-controller.git?path=src/Lhh.TestController.Shared" It contains MagicOnion service contracts and command DTOs used by: Your NUnit tests (LHH_TestSDK in the Editor), The InAppTestRunner code in the player build, The Test Controller process on your machine. Editor, player, shared package, and running controller must all match the version dev released together. If they drift, you may see hub connection failures or RPC errors. Updating after a release When dev ships a new Test SDK: Update com.lhh.testsdk in manifest.json (new tag or commit on lhh-auto-test-sdk). Open LHH Test SDK → Settings → Install Test SDK again so installer-owned dependencies stay in sync. Update com.lhh.testcontroller.shared in manifest.json if release notes pin a new controller tag/commit (for example #v0.2.0). Ask the game team for a new Android APK built with the updated automation bits; update App path in Settings before running tests. Confirm in Window → Package Manager that both com.lhh.testsdk and com.lhh.testcontroller.shared are present. Player build (InAppTestRunner) Tests drive a real Android build on a device. That APK must come from a project that: Includes the Test SDK package (which contains InAppTestRunner—hub + command executors for UI, scenes, PlayerPrefs, IAP, etc.). Has LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST enabled for the Android build target (same define Install Test SDK adds for the Editor; the game team must include it on the player platform). At runtime the player should connect to the Test Controller hub (look for logs such as TestSDK: Create MagicOnionCommandHub Done in logcat when debugging). Bundle ID on the device build must match what you configure in Settings (Player Settings application identifier, or Bundle ID override). Next steps Test Controller and settings—install and start the controller, set gRPC, app path, and platform. Writing test cases Running tests

manual/running-tests.html.title: Running tests | LHH Test SDK
manual/running-tests.html.summary: Running tests Android only until a future release documents iOS. Checklist before Run Test SDK installed in the project (Install the Test SDK). com.lhh.testcontroller.shared present and aligned with the SDK/controller version dev released. Test Controller Running in LHH Test SDK → Settings → Advance Settings (Run Test Server). Android device connected (USB debugging); controller can see it via Appium. Settings filled in: Platform: Android App path: automation-enabled APK (contains InAppTestRunner + LHH_AUTOMATION_TEST on Android) Bundle ID matches the APK (override or Player Settings) gRPC server address: http://127.0.0.1:5050 unless your machine uses another host/port Player build is the version QA expects (rebuild and refresh App path after SDK/shared updates). Run from Test Runner Window → General → Test Runner Select EditMode (or PlayMode if your team uses it for specific tests). Run one test, a fixture, or all tests. On the first LHH_TestSDK call in that run, the SDK performs implicit setup (device lease, Appium session, hub wait). Setup can take tens of seconds—this is normal. When the entire run completes (pass or fail), the SDK returns the leased device automatically. You rarely need to call CleanUpAfterTest yourself. What “good” looks like Unity Console: setup logs, then your test logs/assertions. Device: app launches (if App path set), UI responds to clicks driven from the Editor. No InvalidOperationException for hub not connected or device assignment failed. Troubleshooting Symptom Things to check Command hub is not connected APK built without InAppTestRunner / automation define; wrong bundle id; controller not running; firewall blocking gRPC. Test device assignment failed Another test holding the device; controller not running; no free Android device. Timed out waiting for object/scene Wrong path (use Extract Object Path); object not loaded yet—increase timeout; game not on expected scene. Failed to click button Path not a Button; object inactive; use WaitForObject path first. Purchase failures Use PurchaseByButton / Purchase; store/account sandbox; allow up to 3 minutes for Purchase. Empty app path warning Set App path in Settings; session may not launch the build you intend. RPC / type errors after upgrade Update com.lhh.testsdk and com.lhh.testcontroller.shared, re-run Install Test SDK, restart Test Server, use a new APK. For controller-side logs, see the Progress panel in Settings or logs under ~/lhh-auto-test-controller/.run/ when using the installed controller repo. Reference Scripting API — LHH_TestSDK — full method list and parameters.

manual/test-controller-and-settings.html.title: Test Controller and settings | LHH Test SDK
manual/test-controller-and-settings.html.summary: Test Controller and settings Android only for running tests today. Open Settings LHH Test SDK → Settings Values are stored in EditorPrefs on your machine (not in git). Each QA machine keeps its own gRPC address, app path, and bundle id. Configuration (always visible) Field Purpose gRPC server address Test Controller URL. Default: http://127.0.0.1:5050. Bundle ID Optional override. If empty, the effective id is Player Settings → Application identifier. Must match the installed APK. Platform Use Android for now. App path Path to the automation-enabled .apk. Use Browse to pick the file dev or CI gave you. If App path is empty, setup may warn and the session cannot launch your build. Install and run the Test Controller (recommended) Use the Settings window instead of manual shell scripts. Enable Show Advance Settings. Install Test Controller — clones and prepares ~/lhh-auto-test-controller (runs environment check/setup as needed). Wait until the button shows Test Controller Installed. Run Test Server — starts Appium and the controller (default gRPC 5050, Appium 4723). Status should show Running before you run NUnit tests. When finished for the day, Stop Test Server. If install fails, read the Progress panel in Advance Settings. Missing JDK, Android SDK, or Appium usually requires a one-time machine setup—coordinate with dev/infra; QA’s normal path is still the Install Test Controller button. The running controller version should match the com.lhh.testcontroller.shared package version in your Unity project (see Install the Test SDK). What happens when a test starts The first LHH_TestSDK call in a Test Runner run (for example WaitForObject) automatically: Connects to the gRPC address in Settings. Requests a test device from the controller. Creates an Appium session and launches the App path APK when configured. Waits until the Unity player’s command hub is connected. You do not call setup APIs yourself in normal tests. When the Test Runner finishes the whole run (or reports a runner error), the SDK returns the device to the controller. manual/writing-tests.html.title: Writing test cases | LHH Test SDK
manual/writing-tests.html.summary: Writing test cases Tests are ordinary NUnit tests in the Unity Editor. They call static methods on LHH_TestSDK to control the game on a connected Android device. API details: Scripting API — LHH_TestSDK. Where to put tests Add a test assembly under your project, for example Assets/Tests/..., with references to Unity Test Framework and the Test SDK assemblies (follow how your game repo already sets up Edit Mode tests). Edit Mode vs Play Mode Most automation tests run in Edit Mode so the Editor drives the device while the game runs on hardware: [Test] [RequiresPlayMode(false)] public async Task Example_flow() { await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForScene("Home", timeoutSeconds: 50f); await LHH_TestSDK.WaitForObject("iap_manager"); await LHH_TestSDK.ClickButton("__VIEWS__/Shop/.../Button Open"); } Use async Task test methods and await every SDK call. Typical flow Wait for state — WaitForScene, WaitForObject (poll every 2 seconds until timeout). Act — ClickButton for normal UI; IAP shop buy flows use PurchaseByButton or Purchase. Assert — NUnit Assert.* on values from GetGameData, GetText, or your own helpers. Example reading PlayerPrefs on the device: string raw = await LHH_TestSDK.GetGameData("coin"); Assert.IsTrue(int.TryParse(raw, out int coins)); Assert.GreaterOrEqual(coins, 1000); Hierarchy paths (buttons and objects) Paths use / between hierarchy segments, same rules for WaitForObject, ClickButton, and GetText: Root objects: path segment matches GameObject.Find. Children: resolved with Transform.Find under the previous segment. Copy paths from the Editor: LHH Test SDK → Extract Object Path Or GameObject → LHH Test SDK → Extract Object Path with a object selected. Paste the copied string into your test constants. Real projects often use long paths under prefixes such as __VIEWS__/.... UI clicks vs in-app purchase Goal API Tap a normal Unity UI button ClickButton(path) Tap shop buy + complete native store sheet PurchaseByButton(path) Purchase by store product id (no button path) Purchase(catalogProductId) Do not use ClickButton for IAP buy buttons that must trigger the native store UI—use PurchaseByButton. Logging during investigation These only write to the Unity Console; they do not talk to the controller: LHH_TestSDK.LogWithColor("checkpoint A", Color.cyan); LHH_TestSDK.LogError("coins before assert: " + coins); Timeouts WaitForScene, WaitForObject, ClickButton, and GetText accept optional timeoutSeconds (default 30). Increase for slow loads or heavy scenes. Next step Running tests
